claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you assess your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me: **How many children are you enquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm enquiring about my child. His name is Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're enquiring about your child, Alex.

To help me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask: **How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful.

Now, to continue the assessment: **Are you the person who is responsible for Alex's day-to-day care, or are you enquiring on behalf of someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm responsible for Alex's day-to-day care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, thank you for confirming that.

Next question: **What is your residency status in the UK? Are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or another type of visa or residency arrangement?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a UK citizen and I live here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for that information.

Now, to complete the assessment: **What is your current annual household income?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure what my exact annual income is off the top of my head - why do you need to know that? I thought we were checking if I'm eligible for Child Benefit?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's a fair question! Let me clarify: Child Benefit itself doesn't have an income limit for eligibility. However, I do need to ask about your income for a different reason.

If you're eligible for Child Benefit, there's a separate tax charge called the "High Income Child Benefit Tax Charge" that applies if your household income is over £50,000 per year. This means you could still receive Child Benefit, but you might have to pay tax on it if your income is in that higher range.

So the question helps me give you complete information about your situation. However, if you'd prefer not to share your exact income, could you at least tell me: **Is your household income over £50,000 per year, or below that threshold?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see. No, my income is well below £50,000 a year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for that information. That's very helpful.

Just one more question to complete the assessment: **Is Alex in full-time education or approved training, or does he have any disabilities?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 8, so yes, he's in primary school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit.

Based on what you've told me:
- You're responsible for Alex's day-to-day care
- You're a UK citizen living in the UK
- Alex is 8 years old and in primary school
- Your household income is below £50,000 per year

Let me provide you with my assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Congratulations! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

To summarise why:
- Alex is 8 years old and in primary school, so he meets the age and education requirements
- You are his parent/guardian responsible for his day-to-day care
- You are a UK citizen with UK residency
- Your household income is below £50,000, so there would be no tax charge on the benefit

If you'd like to claim, you can apply through the official government benefits system. Is there anything else you'd like to know about your eligibility?
